objective: Build a small local browser game whose core interaction is immediately legible, mechanically distinct and replayable after a three-minute blind play session.

source_bundle.content: The player routes coloured pulses through a five-node board. Each move rotates one junction. Matching three pulse colours in order blooms the board and advances the score multiplier. A collision rewinds only the most recent junction rotation. The game must run from static local files without a server.

A fresh player should identify routing, sequence matching, blooming multiplier and local rewind through play. The build is judged on clarity, originality, game feel, visual identity and desire to replay.
Add accounts, a backend leaderboard, procedural campaigns and online multiplayer before testing the core interaction.

deliverables: Runnable HTML, CSS and JavaScript files.
A three-minute playtest script and evidence form.
constraints: No build server or remote dependency is required to play.
Do not add backend, accounts or multiplayer.
The collision rewind affects only the latest rotation.
Visual feedback must explain the sequence and multiplier.

completion_checks.description: The game runs from local static files.
Only the locked three-colour order triggers a bloom.
Collision reverses the latest rotation without resetting unrelated state.
No backend, account or network dependency is introduced.
Fresh players identify at least three of four defining mechanics and prefer replaying the final build over the baseline.

evaluator_rubric: The game communicates state through play rather than tutorial walls.
The four mechanics interact rather than appearing as disconnected features.
The build remains scoped and locally runnable.
The critic uses real play evidence rather than screenshots alone.
forbidden_shortcuts: Claiming replay value from the builder’s opinion.
Adding unrelated features to create an illusion of depth.
Replacing interaction with a design document.
Counting an unplayed build as complete.
